title: Mate with king and queen: the supported check
outcomes: Gives checkmate in one with king and queen against a lone king
Says why the queen's check must be protected by the king
Recognises a position where no mate in one exists yet

steps.text: A queen alone cannot finish the game: the lone king simply captures her. Checkmate with king and queen needs three things at once. The queen **gives check**. Every square next to the black king is **covered or occupied**. And the checking queen is **protected**, usually by your own king standing next to her. Look for all three before you move.

steps.caption: White to move: mate in two. The queen cuts the king off, then the white king protects the final check.

line.say: The queen covers the whole seventh rank. The black king has one square left.
Black's only legal move is the king to g8.
Check. The white king on f6 protects the queen, so the king cannot take her. Checkmate.

steps.text: **When it holds, and when it fails.** A queen check is mate only if the king cannot capture the queen and has no free square. The look-alike that fails: the same queen check with your king one step too far away. Before you play a check, ask: *what protects my queen?* Which corner the king sits in changes the route, not the method.

steps.title: Same queen move, the king one step away
steps.prompt: White plays Qg7 in both positions. In the second the white king is on e6 instead of f7. Predict the result each time, then check.
Before your last check, did you ask what protects the queen? Which of the three things (check, no free square, protected queen) did you check last?
